changelog: Backtesting replay keeps loaded candle history across every Next Bar/Play tick instead of discarding it: a plain advance now merges just the new tail bar into the existing array (btLoadCandleWindow()'s new resetView=false path) rather than re-fetching and replacing the whole lead-in window every time.

Scroll-back loading is back on during an active backtest session: dragging left near the oldest loaded bar fetches older candles through the backtest endpoint again (js/chart.js's loadOlderCandles(), re-enabled) -- still clamped server-side to the replay cursor, same no-lookahead guarantee as every other candle fetch in this app, until the symbol's earliest real data is reached.

Added a memory cap on loaded candles (5000 bars) that trims only from the far-left, and only when doing so is safely outside the currently visible window -- a long Play session or an aggressive scroll-back can't grow the array forever, but trimming never disturbs what the trader is actually looking at.

The price axis now refits to whatever's actually visible when the trader scrolls or jumps instead of holding onto a stretched range left over from a different part of history -- the existing 'no vertical bounce' widen-only stabilizer only applies while actively following the replay cursor now; panning away lets Lightweight Charts' own natural per-frame autoscale take over, and a reset happens cleanly on every return to the live edge (Jump to Latest, double-click, or scrolling back by hand).

Fixed the real cause of the reported 'blank 1H view after ~900 bars': a DST 'fall back' transition in the trader's own display timezone (e.g. America/New_York every November) made two different real candles convert to the identical displayed second, which threw inside Lightweight Charts' setData() and left the chart rendering nothing at all. Confirmed via a direct repro (not guessed) and fixed in the one place every candle array is converted before being handed to the chart.
release_notes: No DB migration. Confirmed via git stash + isolated re-runs that this change does not affect: fixed bar spacing (still set once per fresh load, still scrollToPosition()-only on a plain tick), auto-follow/Jump to Latest (unchanged logic, explicitly re-verified never self-pauses across an 890-bar bulk Play run), the no-lookahead clamp (every candle fetch, old or new, still routes through BacktestController::getCandles()'s own replay_cursor_ms ceiling), and the FSA Gate 1 engine (untouched files, its own feed is independent of chartState.candles entirely). Root-caused the reported blank-1H-view bug via a direct Lightweight Charts repro rather than guessing: fed 301 synthetic candles spanning the real 2020-11-01 America/New_York DST fall-back to the actual chart library and reproduced two distinct 'Value is null' page errors and a fully blank chart -- toDisplaySeconds() legitimately produces the SAME shifted second for two different UTC candles during that one real hour of ambiguity a year, and series.setData() requires strictly ascending time values. Fixed in js/chart.js::candlesToSeriesData(), the single place every candle array passes through before setData() -- each shifted second is now clamped to strictly exceed the previous one, nudging forward by whole seconds only during that one hour. This explains '~900 bars' as coincidental to whichever November a given session's own start date plus the trader's own browser timezone happens to cross, which is also why it wasn't reproducible against this harness's UTC-default headless browser until the display timezone was explicitly forced to a DST-observing one. A separate, unrelated theory (a sparse/gapped server response collapsing the chart) was investigated and ruled out: BacktestController::fetchStoredCandles() uses a row-count LIMIT, not a time-window one, so a real gap in the underlying data just reaches further back in calendar time for the same count of real rows -- confirmed by reading the actual SQL, not assumed. History-keeping: btLoadCandleWindow(resetView) now branches -- true (open/resume/rewind/display-timeframe switch, unchanged) does the original full replace; false (a plain advance) fetches just BT_TAIL_FETCH_BARS=5 candles and merges them into the existing chartState.candles via btMergeCandleTail() (equal time = replace the still-forming bar in place, greater time = append, matching BacktestController::getCandles()'s own partial-bar synthesis exactly). btEnforceCandleCap() trims from the front only when the computed safe amount (current visible range's own `from`, minus a 50-bar buffer) is positive -- during an active Play run old history is always off-screen so this is unconditionally safe; while the trader has scrolled back into real history it correctly computes a safe trim of 0 and simply defers, never disturbing the view. js/chart.js's loadOlderCandles() (scroll-back prepend) calls the same cap function and nets its own addedCount against whatever got trimmed in the same tick. Price axis: btInstallPriceRangeStabilizer()'s autoscaleInfoProvider now returns Lightweight Charts' own natural per-frame range unmodified whenever btAutoFollow is false, and btResetPriceRangeStabilizer() is called on every transition back to following (btOnVisibleRangeChange(), plus explicitly in btJumpToLatest() itself since that path sets btAutoFollow=true before the range-change event fires, so the generic transition-detection in btOnVisibleRangeChange() never sees a change there to react to). Verified end-to-end against the acceptance scenario: new tools/ui-harness/drive-v3270.mjs opens a 1H session, Plays ~900 bars (10 real button clicks to anchor the claim against the actual UI, then an 890-bar bulk run via the real btAdvance() function Play's own interval calls, since 900 real DOM clicks would take many minutes under Playwright overhead for no additional signal) confirming bar spacing never moves and auto-follow never self-pauses at any 100-bar checkpoint, draws a rectangle, scrolls back with REAL mouse drags (not API calls) far enough to actually trigger loadOlderCandles() and grow the loaded set further, confirms the rectangle's anchors stay byte-identical throughout and render on-canvas over its own real candles when scrolled back to them, confirms the price axis span stays in the same ballpark as the actually-visible candles rather than a stretched stale range, confirms Jump to Latest still restores everything afterward, and separately reproduces + fixes the DST blank-chart bug. Every pre-existing driver (drive.mjs through drive-v3261.mjs, 12 total, none edited) plus the new drive-v3270.mjs all pass; duplicate-name scan clean; node --check clean on both changed files (no PHP changed this release). drive-v32210.mjs intermittently timed out waiting for a backtest_advance response when run in the full back-to-back suite -- same pre-existing environment flakiness already documented and isolated in the v3.26.1 release notes (confirmed again this release via an isolated re-run passing clean; unrelated to anything touched here, that driver has no mouse/chart.js/candle-loading interaction at all). Not yet verified from this environment, per the user's own note: a real double-click and drag against real BTCUSDT 1H data on the live site -- this environment only has the harness's mock sessions.
